models.author: RAM GANESH E
models.description:
# 🌊 Flood Segmentation using Multi-Modal Satellite Data

## 📌 Overview
This project focuses on accurate flood segmentation using multi-modal satellite imagery combining SAR and optical data. The solution leverages deep learning models with engineered spectral features and ensemble techniques to improve robustness and generalization.

---

## 📂 Model Files
- `best.pth` → UNet++ (EfficientNet-B5) [Primary Model]
- `model2.pth` → UNet (ResNet34) [Secondary Model]

---

## 🧠 Model Architecture

### 🔹 Model 1 (Primary)
- Architecture: UNet++
- Encoder: EfficientNet-B5
- Attention: SCSE
- Role: Main prediction model

### 🔹 Model 2 (Secondary)
- Architecture: UNet
- Encoder: ResNet34
- Attention: SCSE
- Role: Support model for ensemble

---

## 📥 Input Data

Each sample consists of **10 channels**:

### 🔹 Raw Bands
- HH (SAR)
- HV (SAR)
- Green
- Red
- NIR
- SWIR

### 🔹 Engineered Features
- NDWI  = (Green - NIR) / (Green + NIR)
- MNDWI = (Green - SWIR) / (Green + SWIR)
- NDVI  = (NIR - Red) / (NIR + Red)
- SAR Difference = HH - HV

---

## ⚙️ Preprocessing

- Percentile normalization (2% - 98%)
- Clipping extreme values
- Channel-wise normalization to [0,1]

---

## 🎯 Training Details

- Loss Function:
  - CrossEntropy (weighted) + Dice Loss
- Class Weights:
  - `[0.3, 5.0, 1.0]` (to handle class imbalance)
- Optimizer:
  - AdamW
- Input Channels:
  - 10
- Output Classes:
  - 3

---

## 🚀 Inference Pipeline

### 🔹 Test Time Augmentation (TTA)
- Horizontal flip
- Vertical flip
- Averaging predictions

### 🔹 Ensemble Strategy
Final prediction:
Final = 0.8 × Model1 + 0.2 × Model2

### 🔹 Output
- Pixel-wise classification
- Flood mask extracted as:
class == 1

- Converted to Run-Length Encoding (RLE) for submission

---

## 📊 Key Highlights

- Multi-modal data fusion (SAR + Optical)
- Spectral feature engineering
- Class imbalance handling
- Ensemble learning
- Robust TTA inference

---

## ❌ Limitations

- Small flood regions may still be challenging
- Performance depends on quality of spectral indices
- No cross-validation used (single split training)

---

## ⚖️ License

This model follows the **ANRF Open License**.  
Please refer to the official license documentation for usage and distribution terms.

---

## 🔗 Usage Notes

To use this model:
1. Load `.pth` weights
2. Apply identical preprocessing
3. Run inference with TTA
4. Apply ensemble strategy
5. Generate flood mask

---

models.description:
Model Summary
ResNet50-Unet Flood Segmenter: A semantic segmentation model optimized for satellite imagery to identify flooded regions, permanent water, and dry land.

Architecture: U-Net with ResNet50 encoder.

Training Data: ANRF Theme 1 - Phase 2 Satellite imagery.

Results: mIoU > 0.30.

Usage
Used for pixel-level flood mapping from RGB satellite tiles.

Input: [Batch, 3, 512, 512] (Normalized 0-1).

Output: [Batch, 3, 512, 512] (Class logits).

Snippet: model.load_state_dict(torch.load('best_model.pth')).

Failures: Avoid per-image normalization; always resize to 512px to prevent spatial errors.

System
Standalone inference module. Requires 3-channel optical input. Outputs are typically converted to RLE for GIS integration.

Implementation Requirements
Hardware: NVIDIA Tesla T4 (16GB).

Time: ~2.5 hours for 50 epochs.

Software: PyTorch, SMP, Albumentations.

Model Characteristics
Model Initialization
Fine-tuned from ImageNet-1k pre-trained weights (ResNet50 encoder).

Model Stats
Size: ~100 MB.

Params: ~25 Million.

Latency: ~45ms/image on T4 GPU.

Other Details
No pruning or quantization. No PII involved.

Data Overview
Training Data
Publicly sourced multi-spectral satellite imagery. Pre-processing: Global [0, 1] scaling and 512x512 Resized Cropping.

Demographic Groups
N/A (Geospatial terrain data only).

Evaluation Data
80/20 Train/Val split. Validation set tested across diverse urban and rural land covers.

Evaluation Results
Summary
Achieved 0.30+ mIoU. Hybrid Focal-Dice loss significantly reduced false negatives in flood zones.

Subgroup Results
Strong performance on open water; slight confusion in high-density urban shadows (mitigated by TTA and 0.45 thresholding).

Fairness
Defined as spatial consistency across different terrains. Measured via class-wise IoU to ensure flood detection isn't biased toward large rural areas.

Usage Limitations
Not for autonomous life-safety decisions. Requires cloud-free daylight optical imagery for reliable results.

Ethics
Identified risk: Missing flood pixels (False Negatives). Mitigation: Used Focal Loss to over-weight the minority flood class, ensuring higher recall for disaster zones. Released under ANRF Open License.

models.description:
Optimized ResNet50 V2 baseline with 4 key improvements over the original v1: (1) fixed double class weighting  removed loss weights, WeightedRandomSampler handles balancing alone; (2) MixUp alpha reduced from 0.4 to 0.2 for better discrimination between borderline classes ICDAS 1-2 and 3-4; (3) deeper FC head —Linear(2048→512) → BatchNorm → ReLU → Dropout(0.5) → Linear(512→4); (4) 8-transform Test Time 
Augmentation at inference. Together these changes improved Macro F1 from 0.8232 to 0.8470 and accuracy from 0.8043 to 0.8348 over the v1 baseline.

instances.overview:
Optimized ResNet50 V2 baseline with 4 key improvements over the original v1: (1) fixed double class weighting — removed 
loss weights, WeightedRandomSampler handles balancing alone; (2) MixUp alpha reduced from 0.4 to 0.2 for better discrimination between borderline classes ICDAS 1-2 and 3-4;  (3) deeper FC head — Linear(2048→512) → BatchNorm → ReLU → Dropout(0.5) → Linear(512→4); (4) 8-transform Test Time Augmentation at inference. Together these changes improved Macro F1 from 0.8232 to 0.8470 and accuracy from 0.8043 to 
0.8348 over the v1 baseline.

OdontIA ResNet50 v6 is a deep learning model for automated 
dental caries classification using the ICDAS (International 
Caries Detection and Assessment System) scale.

## Architecture
- Backbone: ResNet50 V2 pretrained on ImageNet-1K V2
- Custom FC head: Linear(2048→512) → BatchNorm1d → ReLU → Dropout(0.5) → Linear(512→4)
- Total parameters: 24.5M
- Best epoch: 37
- Val accuracy: 0.8475

## Classes
- ICDAS 0: No caries — healthy tooth
- ICDAS 1-2: Initial enamel caries — early stage
- ICDAS 3-4: Moderate caries — enamel/dentin involvement
- ICDAS 5-6: Severe caries — extensive dentin involvement

## Performance (with Test Time Augmentation — 8 transforms)
| Class | F1 Score |
|---|---|
| ICDAS 0 | 0.8869 |
| ICDAS 1-2 | 0.8043 |
| ICDAS 3-4 | 0.7937 |
| ICDAS 5-6 | 0.9032 |
| Macro F1 | 0.8470 |
| Accuracy | 0.8348 |

## Training
- Dataset: 3,061 intraoral dental images
- Framework: PyTorch + Albumentations
- Optimizer: AdamW (lr=3e-4, weight_decay=3e-4)
- Scheduler: Warmup (5 epochs) + Cosine Annealing
- Regularization: MixUp (α=0.2), Label Smoothing (0.1), Dropout (0.5)
- Balancing: WeightedRandomSampler (no loss weights)
- Training time: ~27 minutes on Colab T4

## Normalization (stored in checkpoint)
- Mean: [0.7722, 0.6914, 0.5951]
- Std:  [0.1178, 0.1677, 0.1693]
instances.usage:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F
import torchvision.models as models
from PIL import Image
import numpy as np
import albumentations as A
from albumentations.pytorch import ToTensorV2

# 1. Build architecture
device = torch.device('cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu')

model = models.resnet50(weights=None)
model.fc = nn.Sequential(
    nn.Linear(2048, 512),
    nn.BatchNorm1d(512),
    nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Dropout(0.5),
    nn.Linear(512, 4)
)

# 2. Load checkpoint — ${FILEPATH} resolves automatically in Kaggle
checkpoint = torch.load('${FILEPATH}', map_location=device)
model.load_state_dict(checkpoint['model_state_dict'])
model = model.to(device)
model.eval()

# 3. Normalization and labels — stored inside checkpoint
MEAN      = checkpoint['mean']
STD       = checkpoint['std']
label_map = checkpoint['inverse_label_map']

# 4. TTA — 8 transforms
tta_transforms = [
    A.Compose([A.Resize(224,224), A.Normalize(mean=MEAN,std=STD), ToTensorV2()]),
    A.Compose([A.Resize(224,224), A.HorizontalFlip(p=1.0), A.Normalize(mean=MEAN,std=STD), ToTensorV2()]),
    A.Compose([A.Resize(224,224), A.VerticalFlip(p=1.0), A.Normalize(mean=MEAN,std=STD), ToTensorV2()]),
    A.Compose([A.Resize(224,224), A.Rotate(limit=(15,15), p=1.0), A.Normalize(mean=MEAN,std=STD), ToTensorV2()]),
    A.Compose([A.Resize(224,224), A.Rotate(limit=(-15,-15), p=1.0), A.Normalize(mean=MEAN,std=STD), ToTensorV2()]),
    A.Compose([A.Resize(224,224), A.RandomBrightnessContrast(brightness_limit=(0.15,0.15), contrast_limit=0, p=1.0), A.Normalize(mean=MEAN,std=STD), ToTensorV2()]),
    A.Compose([A.Resize(224,224), A.CLAHE(clip_limit=3.0, p=1.0), A.Normalize(mean=MEAN,std=STD), ToTensorV2()]),
    A.Compose([A.Resize(224,224), A.CenterCrop(201,201), A.Resize(224,224), A.Normalize(mean=MEAN,std=STD), ToTensorV2()]),
]

# 5. Predict with TTA
def predict(image_path):
    img = np.array(Image.open(image_path).convert('RGB'))
    tta_probs = torch.zeros(1, 4).to(device)
    with torch.no_grad():
        for tf in tta_transforms:
            tensor = tf(image=img)['image'].unsqueeze(0).to(device)
            tta_probs += F.softmax(model(tensor), dim=1)
    probs = (tta_probs / len(tta_transforms)).cpu().numpy()[0]
    return label_map[probs.argmax()], probs

# 6. Run
pred, probs = predict('tooth.jpg')
print(f'Prediction : {pred}')
print(f'Confidence : {probs.max():.2%}')
print(f'All probs  : { {label_map[i]: f"{p:.2%}" for i, p in enumerate(probs)} }')

ResNet101 V2 upgrade over the ResNet50 v6+TTA baseline. 
The only architectural change is the backbone: ResNet50 (25M params, Top-1 80.9%) replaced by ResNet101 V2 (44M 
params, Top-1 81.9%). All other settings remain identical, same deep FC head (2048→512→BN→ReLU→Dropout→4), MixUp 
α=0.2, WeightedRandomSampler balancing, and 8-transform-

Test Time Augmentation. 
The larger backbone improved Macro F1 from 0.8470 to 0.8529 and reduced ICDAS 1-2 misclassifications from 49 to 39 on the test set.

model.load_state_dict(checkpoint['model_state_dict'])
model = model.to(device)
model.eval()

# 3. Setup — normalization and label map are stored inside the checkpoint
MEAN      = checkpoint['mean']
STD       = checkpoint['std']
label_map = checkpoint['inverse_label_map']

# 4. TTA — 8 transforms for robust inference
tta_transforms = [
    A.Compose([A.Resize(224, 224), A.Normalize(mean=MEAN, std=STD), ToTensorV2()]),
    A.Compose([A.Resize(224, 224), A.HorizontalFlip(p=1.0), A.Normalize(mean=MEAN, std=STD), ToTensorV2()]),
    A.Compose([A.Resize(224, 224), A.VerticalFlip(p=1.0), A.Normalize(mean=MEAN, std=STD), ToTensorV2()]),
    A.Compose([A.Resize(224, 224), A.Rotate(limit=(15,15), p=1.0), A.Normalize(mean=MEAN, std=STD), ToTensorV2()]),
    A.Compose([A.Resize(224, 224), A.Rotate(limit=(-15,-15), p=1.0), A.Normalize(mean=MEAN, std=STD), ToTensorV2()]),
    A.Compose([A.Resize(224, 224), A.RandomBrightnessContrast(brightness_limit=(0.15,0.15), contrast_limit=0, p=1.0), A.Normalize(mean=MEAN, std=STD), ToTensorV2()]),
    A.Compose([A.Resize(224, 224), A.CLAHE(clip_limit=3.0, p=1.0), A.Normalize(mean=MEAN, std=STD), ToTensorV2()]),
    A.Compose([A.Resize(224, 224), A.CenterCrop(201, 201), A.Resize(224, 224), A.Normalize(mean=MEAN, std=STD), ToTensorV2()]),
]

# 5. Predict with TTA
def predict(image_path):
    img = np.array(Image.open(image_path).convert('RGB'))
    tta_probs = torch.zeros(1, 4).to(device)
    with torch.no_grad():
        for tf in tta_transforms:
            tensor = tf(image=img)['image'].unsqueeze(0).to(device)
            tta_probs += torch.softmax(model(tensor), dim=1)
    probs = (tta_probs / len(tta_transforms)).cpu().numpy()[0]
    pred  = label_map[probs.argmax()]
    return pred, probs

# 6. Run
pred, probs = predict('tooth.jpg')
print(f'Prediction : {pred}')
print(f'Confidence : {probs.max():.2%}')
print(f'All probs  : { {label_map[i]: f"{p:.2%}" for i, p in enumerate(probs)} }')

models.provenanceSources:
This model was trained from scratch on a custom dataset of intraoral dental photographs collected and labeled by dental professionals at OdontyLab using the ICDAS (International Caries Detection and Assessment System) scoring system.

Base weights: ResNet101 V2 pretrained on ImageNet-1K V2 (torchvision, PyTorch). Fine-tuned end-to-end on 3,061 dental images across 4 ICDAS severity classes.

Training images were captured from multiple intraoral angles (occlusal, buccal, lingual, proximal) using clinical dental photography equipment. All images were labeled by licensed dentists following the official ICDAS-II criteria.

Dataset: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/leonardoaranguiz/tooth-data
Training notebook: https://www.kaggle.com/leonardoaranguiz
Framework: PyTorch 2.10 + Albumentations
